text:
elaine: Short sync: finalizing Dedicated GA SLA language. Main open items: credit formula, canary/fallback semantics, what we promise in contract vs docs, and ops runbook availability. Need alignment today for legal review.

raj: From infra perf numbers: p95=190ms p99=430ms on baseline. Recommend we set contract SLO to p99=500ms with an operational buffer policy rather than a fixed static buffer.

marta: Monitoring side: agree separate external contract triggers vs internal early-warning alerts. Suggest contract trigger = p99 > SLA for 10m OR error_rate > 1% for 5m. Internal alerts fire much earlier (p99 drift or high queue depths).

ben: Credits: legal wants simple wording. My suggestion: linear step formula capped at 25%. Code sample: 

```
credit_pct = min(25, floor(downtime_minutes / 60) * 5)
```

ben: So each full hour -> +5% credit up to 25%. Maintenance with 72h notice = no credit.

claire: Two contract nuances: 1) credits apply to overage/usage charges only (not committed reservation fees), 2) for partial-impact incidents we prorate credits by affected share. We need a clear definition of "affected share" in the annex.

raj: Implementation note: we can compute affected share by looking at successful request counts per tenant/region during incident window. Will add telemetry metrics.

marta: Canary policy proposal: pause if (error_rate > 0.5% for 3m) OR (p99 > SLA_threshold for 5m). On pause -> rollback + route affected traffic to fallback variant + open incident ticket.

elaine: Do we default to blocking fallback unless customer opts in? Many customers expect semantic preservation.

ben: Prefer opt-in for relaxed fallback. Default = preserve semantics; relaxed mode allows quantized/cheaper variants and may drop some advanced features. We'll need explicit consent per-model or per-route.

claire: Contract will say "fallback may be used when customer has opted into relaxed fallback" and reference SDK docs for enabling. Legal happy with that.

ops-bot: canary-started by raj at 1779990060  6/12 nodes  monitoring p95/p99 per-shard.

raj: Canary update: minute 9 -> p99 spike to 580ms on one shard, auto-pause triggered, that shard rolled back, fallback routing exercised for a tiny subset, no customer-visible errors.

marta: Good test. We'll capture anonymized timeline for the runbook example.

elaine: Action items: 
- raj: confirm final p95/p99 baseline and fallback headers (X-Redwood-Fallback) by Tue EOD (1780076400).
- marta: finalize canary triggers and PagerDuty mapping by Tue.
- ben: draft simple credit clause and sample calc for contract annex by Wed.
- claire: write short contract paragraph and reference annex, coordinate with revenue ops by Wed EOD.
- all: add a one-page runbook snippet to docs with the canary failure case.

elaine: If we close these we can ship SLA language and runbooks into the Dedicated contract for GA. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
